messages:
ash: Heads-up: saw a memory-growth/regression on longctx runs that looks like pagetable walk time exploding after repeated evicts. Repro on H100 and MI250x (smaller magnitude on RTX).

kai: can you paste the top-level logs / perf counters?

ash: tl;dr: kvcache used to plateau, now VRAM keeps climbing until OOM or huge page-walk stalls. Attached a short trace snippet. Logs show repeated `kvcache:evict` events followed by bursts in `page_walk_ms` and a slow decline in reuse hits.

ash: snippet:
```
[ kvcache:evict id=0x7f count=64 ]
[ kvcache:alloc page=0x1f4 ]
metric page_walk_ms=23 -> 240 -> 620
metric reuse_hit=0.82 -> 0.47 -> 0.12
```

rachel: hmm that pattern (evict spike then walk slow-down) matches a weird LRU-flattening behavior I saw last week in another job. When PT fragmentation increases, the walk becomes sparse and kernel launch overhead balloons.

benji: do you see the same when you force a smaller batch size / disable batching heuristics? want to rule out batching creating pathological access order.

ash: yes — reproduced with batch=1 and batching disabled. So it's not batch ordering. Also ran with kv_prefetch=off and still saw the growth. The difference across GPUs: H100 shows most severe growth; MI250x shows repeated page remaps with holes in the shadow map.

kai: can you run the ptx trace with `KV_DEBUG=ptwalk=1` and capture a flamegraph? pagerbot, file capture?

pagerbot: captured flamegraph: https://internal/trace/1709876543/fg.svg (auto-attached) :robot_face:

ash: shared flamegraph — the tail shows heavy time in `kv_page_walk_kernel` and a lot of tiny kernels spawned from `kv_rescue_task`. The trace shows a growing number of noncontig page ranges returned by the pagetable walker.

rachel: hypothesis: after repeated evicts, the LRU compaction (we call it "flatten") produces many small free segments; our PT mapper prefers linear chunks and ends up doing many small remaps. That increases kernel count and kernel-launch overhead dominates.

benji: could be. Another angle: the slotmap metadata may have stale owners so the reuse heuristic mis-scores pages as dead and we thrash. Any evidence of stale refcounts?

ash: saw a few logs like `pt:owner_mismatch` but not always. I added an assert and reproduced a case where the slot's owner id changed between eviction and remap (concurrent handoff).

kai: ok, two actionable experiments:
1) change PT mapper to prefer scatter-friendly remap (coalesce up to N small fragments into one remap job) and bench.
2) add lightweight batching of remap kernels (reduce launches by grouping contiguous noncontig fragments into one kernel).

rachel: also add telemetry for `fragment_count` per remap and `remap_kernel_count` per evict cycle — that'll help correlate fragmentation -> kernel explosion.

benji: I can add a quick heap sanitizer that stamps owner ids on alloc/free to catch owner_mismatch more deterministically. I'll do it and run the MI250x repro.

ash: thanks. I pushed a tiny repro harness: `tools/repro/kvcache_frag_repro.py` (local). Steps: allocate longctx tokens ~64k, repeatedly sample random rewrite patterns, trigger evict with `--force-evict`, watch `page_walk_ms`.

kai: assign me to the remap-coalesce change. I'll prototype a `remap_batcher` that groups fragments by target GPU memory region and launches one kernel per group. If perf improves on H100, we have a win.

rachel: timeline? if benji's sanitizer shows owner flips by EOD we can test coalescing tomorrow on CI. Otherwise we'll need a deeper refcount fix first.

benji: starting sanitizer run now on MI250x pool; will post results in this thread.

ash: one more note — kernel-selection heuristics started choosing a smaller tiling kernel for these remaps after the last kernel update. That may increase overhead per fragment. Kai, can you pin the larger tiling kernel in your experiment to isolate kernel-selection impact?

kai: yep, will try both pinned-kernel and dynamic-kernel in the prototype.

ash: thx all. Filing a short issue: infra/kv/1709876543 — adding logs, flamegraph, repro script. Tagging @kai @benji for ownership. :thumbsup:

pagerbot: issue created: https://internal/issue/1709876543 (linked)

benji: SAN run finished: saw ~14 owner_mismatch events over 2hrs on MI250x. I'll attach the dump.

ash: dump looks convincing. Sounds like a race during handoff between async reclaim and allocate path. We'll need both: (A) a short-term remap coalescing + kernel pin to avoid OOM, (B) a correctness patch to prevent owner flips.

rachel: agree. Let's not roll out kernel changes without the sanitizer proving the race is fixed.

kai: starting prototype now, will share perf numbers in this thread.

ash: great — appreciate the quick turnaround.
